chain: Brazil has beacon-regent Lyon, and Brazil also has beacon-regent Oslo. (given in prompt)

'Has beacon-regent' is not functional..why: "Beacon-regent" is a made-up relation (catalogued as has_beacon_regent, fictional, no property tags): nobody uses the phrase and it carries no default sense of how many a country has. The instance countries and cities are real but have no recorded beacon-regency.

Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam..why: The first sentence of the Hanoi article.

Hanoi is in South America..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam, in Southeast Asia.

notes: RBox expansion paired with geography-replace-0018 (which lets a city be the national capital of two countries, i.e. makes 'is the capital of' not functional): a made-up relation, has_beacon_regent (country to city), is given the same property, applied to real countries and cities. Side facts and near and far unrelated queries are those of the revision record. Yes and no: the direct question and the cross-lingual queries ask whether a second value is possible (yes), the first instance asks whether two given values must coincide (no), the second whether a second value could exist (yes). The negation asks whether the relation is functional (no).
